Introduction Here we will discuss about GitHub that:
What is GitHub? Why we use GitHub? How to use GitHub? What is GitHub? Before we know about GitHub, it is important to know about Git and Open-Source Projects.
1. Git Git is a version control system that tracks any changes a developer makes to their projects, enabling them to revert certain changes they made or return to a past version of their project.
2. Open-Source Project Open-Source Projects are, in simple terms, software projects that have their source code open and available to use by anyone.
Here comes GitHub’s role. GitHub is a web-based Git or version control repository and Internet hosting service.
GitHub is the best place to share code with friends, co-workers, classmates, and complete strangers. Over a million people use GitHub to build amazing things together.
Why we use GitHub? GitHub allows developers to host their open-source projects on an online repository to be available for everyone, and uses Git to allow developers to track their projects and collaborate on other people’s projects.
Today GitHub is used by millions of developers and has succeeded in building a huge community where millions of developers from all over the world collaborate on open-source projects.
How to use GitHub? Search for GitHub in your browser.
After doing so, click on the first link.
Enter your Username or email address and password, then click on Sign in.
After that, a dashboard of GitHub will appear.
From here, you can upload files in your repositories and find other users’ repositories as well.

Introduction In this guide, we will explore GitHub, covering:
What is GitHub? Why use GitHub? How to use GitHub? What is GitHub? Before diving into GitHub, it is essential to understand Git and Open-Source Projects.
1. Git Git is a distributed version control system that allows developers to track changes in their projects, revert to previous versions, and collaborate efficiently.
2. Open-Source Projects Open-source projects are software projects where the source code is publicly available, allowing anyone to use, modify, and contribute to the development.
This is where GitHub plays a crucial role. GitHub is a web-based platform that hosts Git repositories and provides version control and collaboration tools.

Why Use GitHub? GitHub offers a cloud-based repository system that enables developers to:
Host and manage open-source projects. Track changes and maintain version control using Git. Collaborate with other developers by contributing to existing repositories. Enhance project visibility and engagement within the developer community. With millions of developers contributing to open-source projects on GitHub, it has become one of the most influential platforms for software development.
How to Use GitHub? Search for GitHub in your browser and navigate to the official website.
Click on the first link in the search results to access the GitHub homepage.
Sign in by entering your username or email address and password, then click Sign in.
Once signed in, you will be directed to your GitHub dashboard.
From the dashboard, you can create repositories, upload files, and explore other repositories to collaborate with developers worldwide.
By following these steps, you can effectively use GitHub to manage your projects and contribute to the open-source community.

Introduction In this guide, we will explore GitHub, covering:
What is GitHub? Why use GitHub? How to use GitHub? What is GitHub? Before diving into GitHub, it is essential to understand Git and Open-Source Projects.
1. Git Git is a distributed version control system that allows developers to track changes in their projects, revert to previous versions, and collaborate efficiently.
2. Open-Source Projects Open-source projects are software projects where the source code is publicly available, allowing anyone to use, modify, and contribute to the development.
This is where GitHub plays a crucial role. GitHub is a web-based platform that hosts Git repositories and provides version control and collaboration tools.
GitHub is widely used for sharing code with colleagues, contributing to open-source projects, and managing software development workflows. Millions of developers worldwide use GitHub to build and maintain projects collaboratively.
Why Use GitHub? GitHub offers a cloud-based repository system that enables developers to:
Host and manage open-source projects. Track changes and maintain version control using Git. Collaborate with other developers by contributing to existing repositories. Enhance project visibility and engagement within the developer community. With millions of developers contributing to open-source projects on GitHub, it has become one of the most influential platforms for software development.
How to Use GitHub? Search for GitHub in your browser and navigate to the official website.
Click on the first link in the search results to access the GitHub homepage.
Sign in by entering your username or email address and password, then click Sign in.
Once signed in, you will be directed to your GitHub dashboard.
From the dashboard, you can create repositories, upload files, and explore other repositories to collaborate with developers worldwide.
By following these steps, you can effectively use GitHub to manage your projects and contribute to the open-source community.
